document.title: perf(runtime): bound input handling per JS loop iteration
document.summary: `process_input_events` stops after about 16 ms of handlers so the JS loop reaches timers, microtasks and the snapshot swap during an input backlog, and a new CTest harness checks the bound.
document.why: When input arrives faster than its handlers finish, the JS loop never leaves the input `while`, so no snapshot is published and [the screen stops updating until the backlog clears](source:s1).

sources.title: perf(runtime): input backlog starves snapshot swaps on the JS thread
sources.gist: Bound the work per JS loop iteration so a slow-handler backlog still publishes snapshots.

lookFor: The ticket's check is [swaps well above 0 in `minesweeper-navigate`](source:s1), which this change cannot show: that scenario's commits make 0 native mutations (focus is native), and on main #125 removed its renders entirely, so `instance_tree_swap` has nothing to publish. The PR proves swaps with a throwaway, uncommitted `minesweeper-flag` scenario instead.

The ticket expects [input latency to stop growing over the window](source:s1). It does not: the budget reorders the same work, so a backlog of slower-than-input handlers still grows; only the screen keeps updating.
The ticket names the Vita baseline; the before/after was measured in Vita3K, and no baseline is updated because no committed scenario moves.

groups.title: Input time budget
groups.why: Bounding per-iteration input work is [the fix the ticket proposes](source:s1).
groups.summary: `process_input_events` stamps a deadline 16 ms out before the first pop and breaks after any event that ends past it, so one event always runs.
lookFor: Subtle: a `pressstart` and its `pressend` can now land in different iterations, with timers, microtasks and a swap between them; the pressed state can paint before the release is handled.

groups.title: input_budget_harness
groups.why: It pins the bound without a Vita: slow handlers must leave events queued, cheap ones must still drain in one call.
groups.summary: `tests/input_budget_harness.c` stubs `vitadeck.input.onPadButtonFromNative` with a busy-wait and calls `process_input_events` directly, and `CMakeLists.txt` builds it from `HOST_RUNTIME_SOURCES` as a CTest.
lookFor: The cheap-handler case asserts 8 trivial calls finish inside 16 ms of wall-clock time; a long preemption on a loaded CI runner would fail it.

commits.subject: chore(runtime): address review on the input budget
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Word the budget comment for handlers under 16 ms, and fail input_budget_harness loudly when its handler stub does not evaluate.

commits.subject: perf(runtime): bound input handling per JS loop iteration
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A backlog of slow input handlers kept the JS loop inside process_input_events, so no snapshot swap ran until the queue drained and the screen froze. Stop after about one frame of handlers and let timers, microtasks and the swap run before the rest.

Fixes #124

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
